title: Coronary Artery Ligation in Mice
author: Mark Kelly LAT
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.56kg9cw

steps.title: Administer Pre-surgical Analgesics
steps.instruction: Approximately 30 minutes prior to the surgical procedure, administer subcutaneous (S.C.) injections of Buprenorphine (0.05mg/kg) and Meloxicam (5mg/kg).

steps.title: Anesthetize and Monitor Mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse using either Ketamine (80-100mg/kg) and Xylazine (5-20mg/kg) or Isoflurane (1-3%).

substeps.instruction: Assess depth of anesthesia at the start of the procedure using a toe or ear pinch.
Perform continuous visual monitoring and periodic toe/ear pinches throughout the procedure, noting any deviations from expected behavior.

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse for surgery using aseptic techniques.

substeps.instruction: Shave the fur around the incision site in the left thoracic area.
Prep the surgical field with 70% isopropanol and Betadine solution, then drape.

steps.title: Intubate and Position Mouse
steps.instruction: Intubate the mouse using a 22-G angiocatheter sheath and place on a rodent ventilator.

substeps.instruction: Position the mouse with the left chest up.
Secure the feet to the surgical area with tape.

steps.title: Perform Left Side Thoracotomy
steps.instruction: Perform a left side thoracotomy between the 3rd and 4th intercostal space.

substeps.instruction: Open the incision approximately 6-7 mm using a small retractor.
Exercise caution to avoid injury to the lung.

steps.title: Ligate the Left Anterior Descending (LAD) Artery
steps.instruction: Identify the LAD coronary artery using a microscope after opening the pericardium and place a 7-0 Proline suture under the artery without entering the left ventricle.

substeps.instruction: Determine suture placement based on desired infarction size: 2mm below the left atrium for 'large', 3mm for 'medium', or 4mm for 'small'.
For acute ischemia: Tie the suture permanently to ligate the LAD.
For ischemia reperfusion: Secure the 7-0 Proline suture over a 3-4 mm piece of PE-90 tubing to ligate the LAD for 30 minutes, then remove the suture to facilitate reperfusion.

steps.title: Close the Thoracic Cavity
steps.instruction: Close the rib cage and dermis while maintaining a path for air evacuation.

substeps.instruction: Place two separate 6-0 Proline sutures to close the rib cage.
Leave a 20g iv catheter sheath between the sutures to evacuate air after closure.
Suture the dermis closed using 6-0 Proline, tissue clips, or surgical glue.

steps.title: Evacuate Air and Extubate
steps.instruction: Remove air from the thoracic cavity and recover the animal.

substeps.instruction: Use a 1-mL syringe attached to the 20g iv catheter sheath to remove air; gently pinch the skin around the sheath and slowly draw back on the syringe while withdrawing the sheath.
Wean the animal off anesthesia and extubate once spontaneous breathing resumes.

steps.title: Provide Post-operative Care
steps.instruction: Administer fluids and analgesics and monitor the animal's recovery.

substeps.instruction: Inject 0.5 ml of 0.9% NaCl subcutaneously to prevent dehydration.
Administer Buprenorphine (0.05mg/kg) every 12 hours for 72 hours post-op.
Administer Meloxicam (5mg/kg) every 24 hours for 72 hours post-op.
Monitor mice 2x daily for the first 72 hours, then at least 3x per week thereafter.
